title: Wing Trailing Edge — Reinforcement of the Fairing Attachment Rib at Outboard Flap Track 3

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Replacement of the flap track fairing attachment rib at outboard track 3 by a reinforced item, with an added cleat that raises the fairing attachment bending mode clear of the approach buffet band.

sections.planning_reason: Elongated fastener holes have been found in the fairing attachment rib at outboard flap track 3 on nine aircraft at their 12-year check, all of them flying a high proportion of short sectors. The mechanism is buffet excitation of the fairing trailing section in the approach flap configuration, which the original substantiation treated as a static case. Once the elongation exceeds 0.6 mm no repair scheme is available and the rib must be changed anyway, so the reinforced standard is offered as the economic answer.
sections.description: The lower rib assembly D5730125554505 at outboard track 3 is replaced by an item with a thicker attachment flange and increased fastener edge distance. A sub-assembly cleat D5730125388807 is added between the rib and the rear spar cap RO324593-41 to shorten the free length of the fairing attachment. The left-hand cleat BRDE298405-27 is retained and re-drilled to the new pattern. Protective sleeving EN479208-64 is fitted where the fairing control rod passes the new cleat, and the flap position sensor target is repositioned 18 mm inboard.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the flap in the extended position and make it safe. Remove the flap track fairing at outboard track 3 on the wing to be worked. Remove the fasteners at the attachment rib and take out the rib assembly D5730125554505. Do an eddy current inspection of the rear spar cap RO324593-41 at every fastener position and report any indication. Install the reinforced rib assembly and position the cleat D5730125388807 between the rib and the spar cap. Drill and ream the cleat pattern into the retained cleat BRDE298405-27 using the jig. Deburr and restore the protective treatment on all new surfaces. Install the fastener set wet with sealant and torque to the values in the accomplishment instructions. Fit the protective sleeving EN479208-64 on the control rod path. Reposition the flap position sensor target and set the clearance. Install the fairing and do the flap operational test through the full travel, checking sensor target clearance at each position. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TTN-88W1 and TTN-88W2 aircraft from MSN T00003 to MSN T00141, that is those delivered before the reinforced rib became the build standard. Aircraft with the CVX-7200 installation on the TTN-88E1 model are not affected, the fairing geometry at track 3 being different.
sections.material_note: Kit K5730-1008-01 covers one wing. Most operators embody both wings in the same visit but this is not required, since each track is an independent installation. Kit lead time is twenty-two weeks. Removed rib assemblies are returned to Aeralis for the fleet monitoring programme.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled base maintenance visit after 18 000 flight cycles, or within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
